author: Marina Vale
summary: Sophie Lark-style crime-family romance: a strong-willed heroine entangled with a powerful, dangerous man from a rival dynasty through an arranged marriage, a debt, or a forced alliance. Taut with danger, family loyalty, power struggles, and enemies-to-lovers friction; for Endless Tales the heat is closed-door and the violence offstage, so the intensity comes from menace, wit, and shifting allegiances.
sentences: Mix of clipped, confident sentences (5-12 words) and longer ones for lavish settings and inner turmoil. Fragments for menace.
pacing: Fast; each scene shifts the balance of power between the leads or between families. Alternating POVs reveal each side's plans, with an action beat (ambush, deal gone wrong) every few scenes.
vocabulary: Modern and polished, with a luxury-and-danger palette: tailored suits, marble, cigar smoke, bodyguards, old-world family terms. Mild profanity at most; no graphic violence vocabulary.
dialogue: About 55%. Verbal sparring as a power play: threats delivered politely, a heroine who refuses to be cowed, and family members speaking in coded loyalty. Clear tags and named POV switches for audio.
narration: Alternating first person (past or present) between heroine and hero. The hero's chapters reveal ruthless calculation softened by protectiveness; the heroine's notice danger, status, and her own defiance.
openings: Opens with a high-stakes setup already in motion: a contract signed, a wedding announced, a hostage exchange, with a bold line of attitude.
scene_endings: Ends on a power reversal, a threat, or a protective act that betrays real feeling.

ending.finale: The couple unites against a common enemy, loyalties are settled, and the hero chooses her over the family code. Ends with them ruling together, the danger contained but not gone.
ending.episode: Ends on danger or betrayal: an assassination attempt, a family member revealed as the traitor, or the heroine discovering what her new husband really did.

signature_moves: Arranged marriage or a debt as the forced-proximity engine
Alternating his/her POV with opposing agendas
A heroine who wins power through cleverness, not rescue
A protective act revealing hidden tenderness
Smoldering tension that cuts to the next morning
avoid: Explicit sex or on-page graphic violence
Glamorizing abuse or coercion; the heroine keeps her agency
AI cliches like 'a dangerous glint in his eyes' on repeat
Making the hero kind too quickly
samples: The contract was four pages long, and my name appeared on every one of them. Not as a signatory. As the payment. "You understand the terms," my father said. It wasn't a question. Across the polished table, Dante Morello didn't look at the paper. He looked at me, steady and unhurried, the way a man looks at a house he already owns. "She doesn't seem pleased," he said. "I'm not," I said. A flicker of a smile. "Good. I'd hate to marry a liar."

DANTE. Three men in the lobby. One by the elevator. One pretending to read a newspaper no one has printed in a decade. I keep my hand at the small of her back and my voice low. "Don't look around." "Why?" she asks, and of course she looks around. "Because," I say, steering her toward the stairwell, "my uncle just broke our truce." She stops walking. "How do you know?" "Because the man by the elevator," I say, "is my cousin."
